terms.meaning: Sending the browser to a different web address automatically.
The page shown when an item does not exist or is not visible to the visitor.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: File setup and imports
sections.what: Describes the helpers and brings in the redirect and not-found tools, the error check, and the user lookup.
sections.why: The header states these helpers are for server page code.
sections.watch_out: The redirect and not-found tools work by throwing special signals, so they must not be caught by generic error handling.

sections.name: pageUserId
sections.title: Signed-in user or redirect
sections.what: Gives the signed-in user's ID, or sends the visitor to the sign-in page.
sections.why: Likely reason: pages that need a user should never render for someone signed out.
sections.watch_out: The redirect ends the rendering at this point, so code after it will not run.

sections.name: orNotFound
sections.title: Hiding missing or forbidden items
sections.what: Waits for a service result. If the service reports that an item is not found or forbidden, shows the not-found page. Any other error is passed on.
sections.why: The doc comment says this avoids revealing whether an item exists.
sections.watch_out: Only the two named codes produce a not-found page, so new codes need adding here to be hidden.

summary: Helpers for server-rendered pages: send signed-out visitors to the sign-in page, and show a not-found page for hidden or forbidden items.
purpose: Keeps page access rules in one place, so pages do not leak whether an item exists to someone who should not see it.
why: The header describes the page role. The comment on the not-found helper says it avoids revealing that something exists.
how: 1) For pages that need a user, looks up the user ID and redirects to the sign-in page if there is none. 2) Wraps a data call so that not-found and forbidden errors show the not-found page. 3) Passes any other error on unchanged.
inputs: The current user ID from the session, and a promise from a service call.
outputs: A user ID, a redirect to the sign-in page, a not-found page, or the original error.
risks: Any other error from the service passes through unchanged, so error pages must handle it. The redirect means a signed-out visitor never reaches the page content.
debug: If a page keeps redirecting to sign-in, check the session. If a missing item shows an error instead of not-found, check the error code the service throws.
